PAPERLESS_PORT.description: Host loopback port the paperless webserver (Web-UI + REST API) binds on. NPM proxies the public `paperless.<publicDomain>` down to this port behind Authelia forward-auth; the #931 PaperlessIngest adapter reaches the REST API on it via host loopback (127.0.0.1:<port>). Default 8000. NB: the servicebay.healthcheck annotation uses the literal 8000 — change it there too if you change this.

PAPERLESS_REDIS_PORT.description: Loopback port the bundled redis task broker binds on. Only reachable inside the shared host netns; change only if it collides with another loopback service.

PAPERLESS_DB_PORT.description: Loopback port the bundled postgres binds on. Only reachable inside the shared host netns; the default is offset from the stock 5432 so it doesn't collide with any other postgres on the box.

PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD.description: Password for the bundled postgres `paperless` user, shared between the postgres and webserver containers. Auto-generated at install; it used to ship as the literal `paperless` (#1297). Postgres applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD only during initdb, so on an already-initialised data dir the role keeps its old password — post-deploy.py converges the role onto this value with ALTER ROLE and restarts the webserver.

PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE.description: OCR / date-parsing language hint (Tesseract lang codes, `+`-joined). Default `deu+eng`. NOTE: paperless's own OCR archive pass is DISABLED (PAPERLESS_OCR_MODE=auto + PAPERLESS_ARCHIVE_FILE_GENERATION=never in template.yml) because its Tesseract regresses rotated German scans to garble (PoC #929) — Solaris's gemma4:12b vision extractor stays the text source and the #931 adapter PATCHes that clean text into paperless. This value only affects date parsing + the UI locale, not OCR.

PAPERLESS_AI_ENABLED.description: Enable paperless's on-demand AI classifier (#1050). Its get_ai_document_classification() builds correspondent/doc-type/tag suggestions from document.content[:4000] — the exact field the #931/#1033 push adapter PATCHes with clean gemma4:12b text — so it works on the pushed text without paperless's own (disabled) OCR. Suggestions are on-demand: the push adapter calls GET /api/documents/<id>/ai_suggestions/ right after patch_content() so they surface for human review in paperless's own UI. Default true.

PAPERLESS_UID.description: Host uid paperless runs its worker + owns the consume/media/data files as. Default 1000 matches the file-share Syncthing share owner so scans dropped into the shared consume dir are readable.

PAPERLESS_GID.description: Host gid paperless owns its files as. Default 1000, matching the file-share share group.

PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY.description: Django secret key for cryptographic signing. Auto-generated at install; never the paperless default 'change-me' value (which causes the webserver to refuse to start in recent paperless-ngx beta releases).

PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER.description: Username of the managed paperless superuser (#1034). paperless-ngx creates this superuser on first boot from PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER/PASSWORD. Paperless is otherwise SSO-only (Authelia remote-user), so this managed admin is the only API-token-bearing account: the solaris post-deploy mints its DRF API token and wires it into the engine so the #931 ingest handoff runs for real. Default `solaris`.

PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password for the managed paperless superuser (PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER). The solaris post-deploy owns the authoritative value: it persists a managed password host-side (like the jellyfin `solaris` credential) and reconciles it on paperless, then mints the admin's DRF API token from it. Auto-generated at install.

PAPERLESS_SUBDOMAIN.description: Subdomain for the paperless Web-UI + REST API. Internal exposure — gets a cert and a LAN-only access list, plus Authelia forward-auth on top: paperless trusts the forwarded Remote-User header (PAPERLESS_ENABLE_HTTP_REMOTE_USER) so there's no second login. The #931 PaperlessIngest adapter does NOT go through this route — it reaches the API on the host loopback (127.0.0.1:PAPERLESS_PORT), bypassing forward-auth with a paperless API token.
